title: Not recommending the business; Eddie Jefferson's murder
summary: He would not recommend a music career and tells of narrowly missing Eddie Jefferson's shooting in Detroit.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. What’s the scene? I mean I go into Central Park now and I hear guys playing their asses off. But they’ve got their cases open for nickels and dimes and quarters and a couple of one dollar bills that they probably put in there themselves. So I don’t recommend getting into the music business. I mean I caught the tail end of it with the guys that were still — I mean not Glenn Miller — but I was on Woody Herman’s band and I was on Maynard Ferguson’s band, I was with Anita O’Day and things like that. I was with Eddie Jefferson the night he was murdered. The singer. I was playing with him in Baker’s Keyboard Lounge. The great vocalese. He was another hero of mine. And he had said that we’re going to go into the Vanguard and this and that and everything was fine, Richie Cole and all this and that. And I walked out of the vestibule of the club on opening night at Baker’s Keyboard Lounge. There was a Lincoln Continental out front. I got to town late. So thank God I got to town late, otherwise Eddie would have been driving with me, riding with me. And I checked into a different hotel around the corner. And I got in my car and drove around the corner, getting ready for a nice week with Eddie, and I turned on the television and it said, “jazz singer Eddie Jefferson was murdered last night in front of Baker’s Keyboard Lounge.” Well I called Richie Cole. So he said, “Danny, you missed it by 30 seconds.” You know if I had got to town later — or earlier – I would have been standing right there. A shotgun took him down. So I just got in the car and drove straight home. I said let me get out of here. Detroit’s not my town with this. But that was with Eddie Jefferson. I loved him. I loved working with him too. But no I can’t recommend going into this business. I mean you’re involved with it. I don’t know. I mean there’s so many guys out there it’s just ridiculous, and girls now, and I don’t know if the race thing is involved. I don’t know. I’m not in the game anymore. I’m not in the competition. I don’t need a gig anymore. I don’t need money.
